Title: Incomplete/Unanchored Regular Expression Validation in CORS Origin Allowed Checker
Analysis:
In the CORS implementation of Traefik's headers middleware (pkg/middlewares/headers/header.go), isOriginAllowed checks if a request's Origin header is allowed using a list of user-configured regular expressions. 
However, because it uses MatchString on the untrusted Origin string without anchoring the regular expressions (or because users might configure unanchored regular expressions), any substring match of a regular expression like '([a-z]+)\\.bar' will match origins like 'https://malicious.domain.bar.attacker.com' or 'https://maliciousbar.com'. 
Additionally, if a user provides an AccessControlAllowOriginListRegex with a wildcard or a partially anchored regex (e.g., `foo.bar`), a lack of careful validation allows attackers to bypass CORS controls. When matched, the Origin is mirrored back in 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin'. Since Access-Control-Allow-Credentials can be configured to true, this allows malicious sites to read credentials-protected responses from the backend.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
For a configuration with AccessControlAllowOriginListRegex = ["([a-z]+)\\.bar"]:
An attacker-controlled website hosted at 'https://attacker.bar.com' sends a request to the Traefik-proxy entrypoint:
```http
GET /api/sensitive-data HTTP/1.1
Host: secure-app.internal
Origin: https://attacker.bar.com
Cookie: session_id=secret_session
```

Because `([a-z]+)\.bar` matches `attacker.bar` inside `https://attacker.bar.com`, isOriginAllowed returns `true` and the exact `Origin` value is mirrored in the response:
```http
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://attacker.bar.com
Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true
...
```
This allows the attacker's script on `https://attacker.bar.com` to read the response body containing sensitive user data.
